summary: AstraGrid is evaluating moving from OpenAI-hosted to Redwood Dedicated for cost and latency predictability. Key concerns are eval parity (answers matching currently used OpenAI models), latency at 8k context windows, compatibility with vLLM/TGI tooling, and enterprise security (KMS, SOC 2). Redwood AE+SE outlined Dedicated and Private options and proposed benchmarks and a security packet.
topics: current stack: OpenAI + vLLM for on-prem experiments
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-13 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Neill (Redwood); Priya Singh, Carlos Mejia, Amira Khan (AstraGrid)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): AstraGrid exploring migration from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated; want parity on existing evals; security and private networking are blockers; next steps: pricing, bench, security docs.

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood. Quick intros?
00:08 Priya: Hi, Priya here, CTO at AstraGrid, we run a few user-facing assistants and some internal classification...
00:16 Carlos: Carlos, lead ML infra, I mostly run our vLLM / TGI stacks for offline evals.
00:22 Amira: Amira, security, will be looking at compliance and KMS stuff.
00:30 Maya: Great - Liam from our SE team will walk through technical fit, I'm the AE so I handle pricing/contract.
00:37 Liam: Hey team, thanks. Quick agenda: current infra & bottlenecks, compatibility questions (OpenAI parity / vLLM/TGI), deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), and next steps.

02:05 Priya: Our motivation: costs are creeping with OpenAI at scale, plus we need more predictable latency for peak hours. We did some on-prem experiments with vLLM + TGI but not ready for production. Curious how Redwood Dedicated compares.
02:28 Maya: Totally - most customers move for cost predictability and control. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and the same API.
02:37 Carlos: Question - we've tuned prompts heavily on gpt-4o (example), outputs/structure matter. How do you handle eval parity? We can't have regressions.
02:55 Liam: Good point. There are two parts: model selection and prompt engineering parity. On Dedicated we offer curated open-models and Redwood-verified profiles; we can run your eval set to measure BLEU/ROUGE or custom metrics against your baseline. Also we support function-calling and streaming to match behavior.

04:10 Carlos: When you say "curated models" - are they exactly identical to OpenAI responses? We've seen tokenization differences and subtle decoding variance with vLLM.
04:24 Liam: Not 1:1. If you're on OpenAI's closed models there will be variance. We mitigate by: (1) running eval parity tests, (2) offering quantized variants that match latency/cost points, (3) fallback routing to hosted variants for any mismatch during rollout. Practically, we create a parity report with sample prompts and delta analysis.

06:00 Priya: Okay - what about compatibility with our vLLM/TGI pipelines? We leverage vLLM for local caching and custom kernels.
06:14 Liam: Redwood Dedicated supports standard model formats and a variety of runtimes. We don't require you to re-engineer vLLM, but when you run on our runtime you'll see differences in kernel selection and attention kernels. For vLLM, many customers run hybrid: vLLM for offline evals and Redwood Dedicated for production inference. We can export checkpoints/compat adapters if needed.

08:45 Carlos: Any gotchas with KV cache and longer context (we push 8k to 32k occasionally)? Latency spikes have been our issue.
08:59 Liam: Our serving runtime optimizes KV cache and attention kernels; for 8k context we tune batching and kernel selection. We'll include a latency profile in the benchmark. Note that batching improves throughput but can increase tail latency; Dedicated allows configurable autoscaling and burst capacity to meet SLOs.

11:20 Amira: Security: we need SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, SOC 2, and a KMS for customer-managed keys. Data residency matters - some logs cannot leave EU. Is that supported?
11:36 Maya: Yes, we offer Private deployments (VPC or on-prem) for stricter controls. Dedicated has encryption at rest and per-customer network isolation; we offer KMS integrations and audit logs. We'll send the SOC 2 and KMS docs.

13:05 Priya: Timeline: we want a pilot in Q1 to avoid vendor lock-in, and ideally a canary rollout for 10% traffic. What does a pilot look like?
13:18 Liam: Pilot typically includes: model onboarding, eval parity run with your prompt set, latency/cost benchmarks, and a canary route for production traffic. We can do A/B routing and automatic fallback to OpenAI if parity issues arise.

15:02 Carlos: Cost questions: how to compare tokens and compute? Our billing is currently opaque because OpenAI bundles compute.
15:14 Maya: We provide token-level cost and per-route/model dashboards. For Dedicated, pricing is reserved capacity plus per-token accounting for overage; Redwood Optimize gives suggestions for batching/quantization to reduce unit cost. We'll share an example pricing sheet.

17:40 Priya: About function calls and structured outputs - we rely on function-calling pattern for tool orchestration. Any differences?
17:55 Liam: We support function/tool calling semantics and structured output constraints. Implementation parity can vary; we'll test your function-calling cases in the eval to confirm behavior.

20:10 Carlos: Who does the migration work - is it our team or Redwood SEs? We have limited bandwidth.
20:24 Maya: Redwood SEs will run the initial onboarding and benchmarks with you; your infra team will validate the canary. For Private/on-prem installs we have a deployment team and partner installers.

22:00 Amira: Logs/audit access - can we ship logs to our SIEM? We need raw request IDs and redaction options in logs.
22:12 Liam: Yes, we have configurable log exports and redact options. For Dedicated Private you can ship logs to your SIEM via secure connectors. We'll include a sample log schema.

24:30 Priya: About eval parity again - can we get a tolerance threshold? Like X% acceptance for intent/recall?
24:44 Liam: Absolutely. We define pass/fail thresholds per eval metric. We'll run baseline vs Redwood model variants and highlight deltas per prompt. If delta exceeds threshold, we iterate on prompt tuning or try a different model variant/temperature.

27:05 Carlos: Any risk with TGI/vLLM integration - like model weights format or tokenizer mismatch? We've seen tokenization split differences causing downstream extraction issues.
27:26 Liam: Tokenizers can differ; we recommend exporting tokenization used in your current pipeline and we can align tokenizers or provide mapping layers. In worst case you run a lightweight adapter to normalize tokens. We'll test a few representative prompts you provide.

30:00 Maya: Quick recap of options: Hosted API if you want minimal lift; Dedicated for reserved capacity with predictable throughput; Private/VPC if you need customer-managed networking and on-prem controls.
30:18 Priya: We're leaning Dedicated first, Private later if compliance requires. Main blockers: eval parity and security docs.

32:10 Carlos: Bench specifics - can you run 8k context end-to-end with our prompt set, measure p95 latency, token cost, and compare against our current OpenAI numbers? Also include a vLLM local run for parity.
32:28 Liam: Yes - we'll run p50/p95/p99 latencies, token cost, and throughput. We'll include config for batching, KV cache, and quantization variations. Expect initial results in ~5 business days.

35:00 Amira: On contractual side, do you support data retention limits and contractual indemnities for data processing?
35:12 Maya: We have enterprise SLAs and can include retention clauses and DPA terms; specifics depend on the contract tier. I'll share a contract template.

37:40 Priya: Example prompts - I'll upload a small eval corpus to your secure S3 share?
37:52 Maya: Yes, we can provide a secure upload link or you can share via your internal transfer to our SE. We'll mark it private and limit access.

39:20 Carlos: One more technical - can we run mixed workloads (realtime chat + batching for async tasks) on same Dedicated pool?
39:34 Liam: Yes, routing policies can prioritize low-latency queues for chat and batch queues for async inference. Autoscaling and burst capacity can handle mixed workloads.

42:00 Maya: Next steps recap - I'll send pricing, SOC2/KMS docs; Liam will run bench and share parity report; Amira to send compliance questions; we'll schedule technical deep dive for private/VPC.
42:15 Priya: Sounds good. Any blockers from our side other than eval corpus and compliance Qs?
42:25 Carlos: Resource-wise we should be okay for a pilot.
42:30 Amira: I'll circulate the compliance list by Wed.

47:10 Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email with artifacts and a calendar invite for the deep dive.
47:17 Priya: Thanks all.
47:20 End of recording

Notes: transcription contains minor errors - speaker attributions may be approximate; references to vLLM/TGI tokenization intentionally included to mirror customer's phrasing.
